- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast is significantly above recent history, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is below recent history, increase forecast by 5–10% to counteract pessimism.  
- If forecast spikes sharply after a recent high, apply a 1–2 day lag correction: reduce forecast by 10–15% for the next 2–3 days.  
- If forecast mean is consistently above true outcome over 3–5 days, apply a downward bias correction: subtract 2–5% from next 3–5 day forecast.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.3–0.7) and forecast deviates > 3% from true, align forecast to 3-day moving average of true values.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows early mean reversion (first 5–7 days), adjust forecast to reflect downward trend early, not late.
